comments.text: Over 20 years in this house I've gone from electric to induction to finally owning my dream oven, a gas wolf. Induction and electric are whole orders of magnitudes easier to clean. If you're on electric or induction now and considering the switch to gas, do not underestimate that. It's way harder than i imagined. That said, there is something about having the gas that makes the whole process of cooking just much more fun and challenging and engaging. Sometimes i don't really feel like cooking and I'll walk into the kitchen and see those red knobs and iron grates and I'll just get inspired, so don't underestimate that part either. I swear that thing just looks at me sometimes and says "cmon man, let's do this!!".
This was a really excellent video which covered a whole range of cooking related topics.  Please keep those videos coming.
I like very much my YOSUKATA 13.5" carbon steel wok with flat bottom. Nice heat conduction, solid but not too heavy, very nonstick if you keep it seasoned, and only $58 on Amazon. Could last forever.

40:35 as a foodie but also a “if it can’t go in the dishwasher, I don’t want it” guy, I find the green Shapton whetstone will easily put a great edge on midrange beater knives. If you’re worried about messing up, you can’t really dull an average kitchen knife more than it already is, so it’s a great way to learn! Even sloppily done it will cut loads better than it did before. I sharpen mine once a month and chuck em in the dishwasher. My super nice knife is only used for carving, presentation, and sushi a couple times a year.

What a treat to find another Q&A!  I love getting all these random bits of information from someone who knows their stuff. I have a request and hope that it isn't too niche for your audience:  Cooking with pasture raised, heritage breed chicken.  Specifically, NOT the Cornish Cross breed that is ubiquitous in the stores. I've cooked them a couple of times and because they are healthy, active, mature chickens, they can be kind of tough.  I know they can be pan-fried with great results because my gramma used to do it.  But I haven't cracked the code. How bout a doing a deep dive into pan fried heritage chicken? (not literally; that would be painful)
